newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says U.S. not stealing Gulf of Mexico oil.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says U.S. not stealing Gulf of Mexico oil.

text.p: The head of Mexico's state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) on Thursday rejected opposition charges that the United States is drilling from Mexico's side of the Gulf of Mexico.
Pemex's Adrian Lajous Vargas was responding to persistent charges from an opposition party senator that U.S. drilling has impinged on Mexico's area of the shared gulf.
Lajous told an oil engineers conference in the central state of Zacatecas that the size of Pemex's wells would make usurping petroleum difficult, a Pemex statement issued in Mexico City said.
"In any case, Pemex will follow and be alert to any drilling activities on the Rio Bravo border," he added.

Lajous was responding to accusations by opposition senator Jose Angel Conchello that the United States is drilling in Mexico's Gulf territory. Local press have run headlines such as "U.S. steals our oil" following Conchello's charges.
Mexicans are sensitive to any hint of U.S. claims to Mexican oil, and still recall with pride the nation's nationalization of its hydrocarbon reserves almost 60 years ago.
